messages:
maria: quick q — planning to rotate a KMS key and add an IRSA grant for the billing-service sa. want to make sure terraform apply ordering won’t leave pods throwing decrypt errors. what sequence worked for you before?

kai: high level i usually do: 1) update key policy/grant 2) create/attach iam role/trust for k8s sa 3) rollout deployment so new pods pick up creds. do the policy/grant change first so sts assume + decrypt is allowed.

maria: got it. i have a PR that adds an aws_kms_grant resource and updates the key policy. then another tf change to create the eks iam role + aws_iam_role_policy_attachment. any gotchas with having those split across two applies?

kai: split is fine but be careful about race if you apply role before grant. pod could assume role -> call decrypt -> fail if grant not yet present. if you must split, add a small manual hold: apply key changes first, wait for aws propagation (~30s), then apply role changes. also consider depends_on in TF so grant depends_on key, and role change depends_on grant if in same plan.

sienna: fwiw we used this pattern: create aws_kms_grant resource + set `retire_on_delete = false` so revocation is explicit. then in the service account rollout we annotated like `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/billing-svc` only after grant applied.

noah: small terraform snippet that worked for us:```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "billing_irsa" {
  name              = "billing-irsa-grant"
  key_id            = aws_kms_key.billing_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.billing_irsa_role.arn
  operations        = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  retiring_principal = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/admin"
}
```

maria: thanks. any extra IAM condition we should add so only pods from the specific k8s sa can use the key?

kai: yes add Condition on the key policy or grant that checks `sts:ExternalId` or `aws:SourceAccount`/`aws:SourceArn`. for IRSA we put a condition on the trust policy + KMS key policy using `StringEquals": {"sts:ExternalId": "system:serviceaccount:billing:billing-sa"}` — though ExternalId can be tricky. alternatively guard by `kms:EncryptionContext:aws:something` if you set that from the app.

sienna: also remember the session name length/characters. STS session names can be truncated and that breaks any exact-equals conditions. prefer startsWith or contains if you match on session name.

maria: good call. for the kubernetes bit i was going to helm upgrade - we should hold the helm rollout until after role/grant are in place. example annotation i will add:```yaml
serviceAccount:
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/billing-irsa-role"
```

noah: test plan: 1) terraform apply key + grant in staging 2) sanity pod that just calls kms:Encrypt/Decrypt inside same ns 3) once ok, apply role/trust + helm upgrade 4) monitor decrypt errors in logging for 10m canary.

maria: ok i’ll split the PRs accordingly. can someone run the staging apply tonight? prefer a low-traffic window.

kai: i can do staging at 21:00 PT. will watch CloudTrail for GrantCreate events and the pod logs.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary window: 2024-11-02T21:00:00-07:00 for channel eng-infra — will post when terraform starts and when helm rollout begins. :robot_face:

maria: perfect, thanks all. i’ll tag the PRs and post links shortly.

sienna: ping if you want me to async review the key policy JSON before you apply. I can check the conditions and avoid overly strict equality. :ok_hand:

maria: will do — PRs incoming.
